title: I made a plush toy-box platformer where every level has a 12-character code you can swap with friends
author: 0xe25f
selftext:
Hello👋

I’m more of a regular on the Discord than the Reddit, so greetings from the other side!

(I haven’t used AI to write this post, and there are no affiliate links.)

I've been building [Fifth Maker](https://play.fifthdoor.com/play/fifth-maker?referrer=share), a cosy 2D platformer where the whole world looks like handmade toys. You play as Pip, a plush goblin with googly eyes and a fanged grin, and run through stages made from felt, wooden blocks, papercraft and clay.  


**Background / How it was done:**

There was an interesting discussion on the [Discord](https://www.reddit.com/r/aigamedev/comments/1shiykx/ai_game_dev_discord/) a week ago regarding **AI prompt-to-game platforms** and whether they are worth trying or if they're just toys for children. That inspired me to try to make a cosy platform game featuring plush toys and see if it could be a complete game rather than a sloppy tech demo.  
  
I settled on [Fifth Door](https://play.fifthdoor.com/play/fifth-maker?referrer=share) (I’m not affiliated) because it really understood my beastly prompting best out of the bunch I tried; although [Build With Star](https://buildwithstar.com/) came close. Fifth Door also did a bang up job of converting my images to 3D-looking characters with rather little fuss compared to many platforms.

I'm pretty sure they're using Anthropic APIs under the hood, though I'm also sure they've got some witchcraft python scripts going on too - because the art pipeline is top notch. They've also set up a Trailer Maker, which seems to use Seedance and a few python scripts too.

  
So I created a prompt/plan for Fifth Maker using my own Claude sub, with Sonnet 5 Medium, though I dare say it should be Opus 5.5 Low now, ensuring to make it as detailed and thorough as possible.  
I supplied my goblin sketch to GPT 5.6 and had it convert to a goblin character - which in turn I then fed to Fifth Maker as a reference image. I also poached a couple of reference images based on characters made by someone at Fifth Door (I hope they don't mind!). The idea there being that Pip, the goblin, is the Fifth Maker. 😅

Then after it's built the game to the best of it's ability, I was iteratively working through it with the prompting engine; keeping it on track with it's art direction, and doing a thorough amount of testing to ensure all adventure levels are completable, bosses beatable, and settings settable.

  
When I received feedback, such as "I find the background movement jarring", I added an option to the settings menu to disable that. The idea is that the game is challenging, not annoying, and that anyone can jump in.

  
So without further adieux..



**What's in Fifth Maker:**

* **32 Adventure stages** across four storybook worlds: Clover Meadow, Lantern Burrows, Bubble Lagoon and Cloud Castle. Each book ends with a three-hit guardian fight.
* **Unlock friends**. By completing adventure world biomes - you can play as **four additional characters**!
* **Generate:** press a button and you get a fresh stage. Every generated stage has a **12-character share code**, and the same code always builds the same level. Found a brutal one? Post the code and let others suffer too.
* **Two editors.** Workshop is a full freeform tile editor for your personal levels. **Blueprint Mode builds levels that can be shared using a share code**, so you can hand-tune a stage and pass it around.
* **Options for everyone**, so you can play the game cosy and relaxed, or time attack, reduce background movement, change depth of field, and more.
* **Proper platforming feel:** variable jump height, sprint, coyote time, jump buffering, skids, and power-ups that take Pip from Small to Super to Starlight.
* **24 achievements**, a narrated How to Play guidebook, key rebinding and an Options menu with plenty to tweak.

  
It's free and runs in the browser on desktop and mobile (turn your phone sideways). It supports touch, keyboard/mouse and Xbox controllers.

**Play here:** [https://play.fifthdoor.com/play/fifth-maker?referrer=share](https://play.beta.fifthdoor.com/play/fifth-maker?referrer=share)

That is a nicely styled and consistent art style but the character is a little stiff.

I agree the background movement should be tamed, a lot just for a jump.
